data.description:
## Description
**What**: Implement plugins/dso/hooks/check-pipefail-grep.sh as a thin wrapper over static-defense-lib.sh that detects both bare-pipeline and command-substitution/subshell forms of `… | grep -q` under `set -o pipefail`, ships its initial per-hook baseline capturing the ~63 current violations, and registers in .pre-commit-config.yaml between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate. This is the first hook end-to-end and proves the full pattern (detection + baseline + diagnostics + suppression + fixture + dogfood) before replication.
**Why**: SIGPIPE-under-pipefail is the highest-volume and growing class (~63 files, up from 42); blocking new instances stops growth while the shrink-only baseline lets the backlog through.
**Scope**:
- IN: the hook, its detection logic for both forms, its initial baseline, its .pre-commit-config.yaml entry, and its fixture + end-to-end test.
- OUT: remediation of the ~63 existing violations; the other three hooks; the shared library functions (consumed from draft-1).

## Done Definitions

- check-pipefail-grep.sh, when staged content adds a `… | grep -q` under pipefail in bare-pipeline form or command-substitution/subshell form, blocks the commit and the other form is also detected ← Satisfies: sc-1
- check-pipefail-grep.sh reads its per-hook count-based baseline so the captured existing violations do not block, while a new instance beyond the baseline count is blocked ← Satisfies: sc-2
- check-pipefail-grep.sh emits a per-file diagnostic naming the offending line, the remediation string, and the SIGPIPE originating-ticket citation ← Satisfies: sc-3
- check-pipefail-grep.sh honors a `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` suppression with a non-empty token and rejects an empty or whitespace-only suppression reason ← Satisfies: sc-5
- a fixture test asserts detection on staged content, baselined-violation non-firing, new-instance blocking, and baseline-growth rejection; an end-to-end test invokes the hook through the real pre-commit framework and the hook resolves its own path and baseline without CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and passes its own check (dogfood) ← Satisfies: sc-6
- check-pipefail-grep.sh and its baseline resolution execute under a bash-3.2-constrained test that passes ← Satisfies: sc-8
- unit tests (fixture-based) are written and passing for all new detection logic in check-pipefail-grep.sh ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [Hermeticity] The hook MUST resolve its own path and baseline via BASH_SOURCE -> readlink -f, never CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.
- [Build] check-pipefail-grep.sh and its new test files must have the executable bit set.
- [Merge-safety] Register as a discrete, independently-named entry in the shellcheck-to-pre-commit-review-gate band so concurrent hook-adding epics merge without conflict; keep the ordering-invariant comment.
- [Correctness] Command-substitution/subshell form is the documented high-risk false-negative; the fixture suite must include that form explicitly.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a committing developer, I want check-pipefail-grep.sh to block staged scripts that introduce `… | grep -q` under pipefail (bare-pipeline and command-substitution/subshell forms), so that new SIGPIPE-on-Linux antipatterns are caught at commit time.
